questions.stem: Why does the woman say she can be so energetic?
questions.stemZh: 女士为什么说她能如此精力充沛?
questions.answerText: She can devote all her life to pursuing her passion.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Oh, well, I just love what I do. I'm extremely fortunate to have this life, doing what I love doing. 哦，这个嘛，我就是热爱我所做的事。我极其幸运能拥有这样的生活，做着自己热爱的事。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者的直接应答。男方上一句问她"哪来这么多精力"，女方紧接的应答 I just love what I do 就是答案句——对话题里，问句之后被问者的第一句正面回应往往就是落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I just love what I do ↔pursuing her passion love what I do = pursuing her passion doing what I love doing ↔devote all her life to pursuing her passion 一生热爱 ↔ devote all her life

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 Her accumulated expertise helps her to achieve her goals. 里的 expertise 来自后文第 6 段 no matter how much expertise they may already have，但那是在谈教学的好处， 与"为何有精力"无关，是把别处原词搬来骗选。 借用原文：no matter how much expertise they may already have C) 张冠李戴 She can spread her academic ideas on a weekly TV show. 的 weekly TV show 出自男 方提问 you have your own weekly TV show on science，那只是介绍她的身份背景，并 非她解释精力来源，张冠李戴。 借用原文：you have your own weekly TV show on science D) 未提及 Her research findings are widely acclaimed in the world. 借了 research、world 这类访 谈高频词，但全文从没说她的研究成果"广受赞誉"，属未提及，更答非"为何有精力"。

questions.stem: What has the woman been engaged in?
questions.stemZh: 女士一直从事什么工作?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Well, as you said, I do have different things going on. But these, I think, can be divided into two groups: the education of science and the further understanding of science. 嗯，正如你所说，我手头确实有不少不同的事。但这些，我认为，可以分成两大类：科学教 育，以及对科学的进一步理解。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 归并信号 divided into two groups。她用 can be divided into two groups 把零散事务 收成两类，这种"归类"句正是回答"主要从事什么"的落点；冒号后两项就是答案核心。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: the education of science and the further understanding of science ↔ Science education and scientific research education+understanding ↔ education+research

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 Provision of guidance for nuclear labs in Europe. 借男方介绍里的 a senior advisor at the European Organization for Nuclear Research，但那只是她诸多身份之一，不是她 对"从事什么"的总括，以偏概全。 借用原文：a senior advisor at the European Organization for Nuclear Research B) 原词陷阱 Touring the globe to attend science TV shows. 把男方提到的 tour the globe tirelessly, giving talks 和 weekly TV show on science 两件事拼一起，既非她的归类、内容也被改装 （去做讲座变成去上电视秀），原词陷阱。 借用原文：tour the globe tirelessly, giving talks C) 原词陷阱 Overseeing two research groups at Oxford. 里的数字 two 与地名 Oxford 极具迷惑性， 但原文只说她是 a professor of physics at the University of Oxford，从未提"管两个研究 组"，数字属无中生有。 借用原文：a professor of physics at the University of Oxford

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the benefit teaching brings to her?
questions.stemZh: 女士如何评价教学给她带来的益处?
questions.answerText: A better understanding of a subject.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Also, what I will say is that teaching a subject helps me comprehend it better myself. I find that it furthers my own knowledge when I have to explain something clearly. 另外，我想说的是，教一门学科能帮助我自己更好地理解它。我发现，当我必须把某件事讲 清楚时，这会增进我自己的知识。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 受益句 helps me comprehend it better。她用 teaching a subject helps me comprehend it better myself 直说教学的好处，helps me 是受益标志句，答案就锁在 这里。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: helps me comprehend it better ↔A better understanding of a subject comprehend better = better understanding

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 过度推断 A stronger will to meet challenges. 看似呼应第 6 段 Teaching at a high level can be very stimulating，但 stimulating 指"令人有激情/受激励"，并非"更强的迎难意志"，属过 度推断。 借用原文：Teaching at a high level can be very stimulating C) 偷换概念 A broader knowledge of related fields. 借了她说的 furthers my own knowledge 里的 knowledge，但她讲的是同一学科理解"更深"，C 却改成相关领域"更广"，深被偷换成广。 借用原文：it furthers my own knowledge D) 未提及 A closer relationship with young people. 像是从 aid others in understanding it 联 想"帮助别人 拉近关系"，但原文谈的是教学增进她自己的理解，从未说"与年轻人关系更 近"，未提及。

options.textZh: 对某一学科有更深入的理解。

options.label: B
options.text: A stronger will to meet challenges.
options.textZh: 迎接挑战的意志更加坚强。

options.label: C

questions.stem: How does the woman say new scientific breakthroughs can be made possible?
questions.stemZh: 女士认为如何才能实现新的科学突破?
questions.answerText: By making full use of the existing data.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: In fact, right now we have too much data sitting in computers. We have them, yet nobody has had time to look at them with their own eyes, let alone analyze them. 事实上，眼下我们有太多数据躺在电脑里。我们手握这些数据，却没人有时间亲眼看过它 们，更别说分析了。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 现状落差暗示出路。她强调 right now we have too much data sitting in computers 却 nobody has had time to look at them——点出"数据已有、只是没人去用"的落差，言下 之意突破靠把现有数据用起来。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: we have too much data sitting in computers ↔making full use of the existing data 已有大量数据 ↔ existing data nobody has had time to look at them with their own eyes, let alone analyze them ↔ making full use of the existing data 没人去看分析 ↔ 该 full use

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 By applying the latest research methods. 听起来合理，但原文谈的是"数据已有、没人去 看"，从未提"用最新研究方法"，无中生有。 C) 偷换概念 By building upon previous discoveries. 像是呼应 there are constantly new things being discovered 里的 discovered，但她的重点是"用好已有数据"，不是"在前人发现上加 盖"，借 discover 一词擦边偷换。 借用原文：there are constantly new things being discovered D) 原词陷阱 By utilizing more powerful computers. 直接抄了录音里的 computers（data sitting in computers），但电脑在原文只是"数据存放处"，她从没说要"用更强的电脑"，听到 computers 就选正中圈套。 借用原文：we have too much data sitting in computers 1 M: Do you think dreams have special meanings? M: 你觉得梦有特殊含义吗？ 2 W: No, I don't think they do. W: 不，我觉得没有。 3 M: I don't either. But some people do. I would say people who believe that dreams have special meanings are superstitious, especially nowadays. In the past, during the times of ancient Egypt, Greece or China, people used to believe that dreams could foresee the future. But today, with all the scientific knowledge that we have, I think it's much harder to believe in these sorts of things. M: 我也不这么认为。但有些人相信。我会说那些相信梦有特殊含义的人是迷信的，尤其是在现在。在过 去，在古埃及、希腊或中国时期，人们曾经相信梦能预见未来。但今天，有了我们掌握的所有科学知识， 我认为要相信这类事情就难多了。 4 W: My grandmother is superstitious, and she thinks dreams can predict the future. Once she dreamed that the flight she was due to take the following day crashed. Can you guess what she did? She didn't take that flight. She didn't even bother to go to the airport the following day. Instead, she took the same flight but a week later. And everything was fine, of course. No plane ever crashed. W: 我奶奶很迷信，她认为梦能预测未来。有一次她梦到自己第二天要坐的航班坠毁了。你猜她怎么做 的？她没坐那个航班。第二天她甚至都没去机场。相反，她坐了同一个航班，但是一周之后的。结果当然 一切都好好的，没有飞机坠毁。 5 M: How funny! Did you know that flying is actually safer than any other mode of transport? It's been statistically proven. People can be so irrational sometimes. M: 真有意思！你知道吗，坐飞机实际上比任何其他交通方式都安全？这在统计学上已经得到证实。人们 有时候真是太不理性了。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 6 W: Yes, absolutely. But even if we think they are ridiculous, emotions can be just as powerful as rational thinking. W: 是的，完全同意。但即使我们觉得它们很荒谬，情感有时可以和理性思考一样强大。 7 M: Exactly. People do all sorts of crazy things because of their irrational feelings. But in fact, some psychologists believe that our dreams are the result of our emotions and memories from that day. I think it was Sigmund Freud who said that children's dreams were usually simple representations of their wishes, things they wished would happen. But in adults, dreams are much more complicated reflections of their more sophisticated sentiments. M: 没错。人们会因为非理性的感受做各种疯狂的事。但实际上，一些心理学家认为我们的梦是当天情感 和记忆的结果。我记得好像是Sigmund Freud说过，儿童的梦通常是他们愿望的简单呈现，是他们希望 发生的事情。但在成年人身上，梦是他们更复杂情感的更为复杂的反映。 8 W: Isn't it interesting how psychologists try to understand using the scientific method something as bizarre as dreams? Psychology is like the rational study of irrational feelings. W: 心理学家试图用科学方法去理解像梦这样奇异的东西，这不是很有趣吗？心理学就像是对非理性感受 的理性研究。

options.label: A
options.text: By applying the latest research methods.
options.textZh: 通过应用最新的研究方法。

options.label: B
options.text: By making full use of the existing data.
options.textZh: 通过充分利用现有数据。

options.label: C
options.textZh: 通过在先前发现的基础上进行研究。

options.label: D
options.textZh: 通过使用更强大的计算机。

questions.stem: What do both speakers think of dreams?
questions.stemZh: 两位说话者对梦的看法是什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: M: Do you think dreams have special meanings? W: No, I don't think they do. M: I don't either. 男：你觉得梦有特殊含义吗？女：不，我觉得没有。男：我也不觉得有。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者的直接应答。男方一开口就问"梦有无特殊含义"，女方 No, I don't think they do. 是直接应答，男方紧接 I don't either. 表示"我也不"，一问两答把双方立场都钉死，这正是 答案句信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: No, I don't think they do. ↔They have no special meanings. 否定提问=否定其内容

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 They can predict future events. 抓的是录音 dreams could foresee the future，但那是 男方转述"古人曾经相信"的旧观念，并被他用 much harder to believe in these sorts of things 否定，不是两人现在的看法。 借用原文：people used to believe that dreams could foresee the future C) 未提及 They have cultural connotations. 听上去高级，但录音通篇没说梦有"文化内涵"，cultural connotations 是凭空添加，无任何对应句。 D) 答非所问 They cannot be easily explained. 录音从未说梦"难以解释"；两人讨论的是梦有没有特殊 含义，而非解释难度，与他们表达的看法不符。

options.label: A
options.textZh: 梦能够预测未来事件。

options.label: B
options.textZh: 梦没有特殊含义。

options.label: C
options.textZh: 梦具有文化内涵。

options.label: D
options.textZh: 梦无法轻易解释。

questions.stem: Why didn't the woman's grandmother take her scheduled flight?
questions.stemZh: 为什么这位女士的祖母没有乘坐预定的航班?
questions.answerText: She dreamed of a plane crash.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Once she dreamed that the flight she was due to take the following day crashed. Can you guess what she did? She didn't take that flight. 有一次她梦见自己第二天要坐的那班飞机坠毁了。你猜她怎么做？她没坐那班飞机。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果叙事链。女方先说 she dreamed that the flight… crashed（梦见坠机），紧接 She didn't take that flight.（于是没坐），前因后果一气呵成，"梦见坠机"就是没坐航班的原 因，是本题答案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: she dreamed that the flight she was due to take the following day crashed ↔ She dreamed of a plane crash. 长句概括为短句

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 It was canceled due to bad weather. 录音从没提天气或航班被取消，是凭空编出的常见 原因，无对应句。 B) 答非所问 She overslept and missed the flight. 录音明说 She didn't take that flight.（主动选择不 坐），而非睡过头错过；"主动不坐"和"被动错过"性质相反。 D) 原词陷阱 It was postponed to the following day. 偷了录音里的原词 the following day，但原文 the following day 是说"她原本第二天要坐"，且她是改坐一周后的航班，根本不是航班被 推迟到第二天。 借用原文：the flight she was due to take the following day

options.label: A
options.text: It was canceled due to bad weather.
options.textZh: 航班因恶劣天气被取消了。

options.label: B
options.text: She overslept and missed the flight.
options.textZh: 她睡过头了,错过了航班。

options.label: C
options.text: She dreamed of a plane crash.
options.textZh: 她梦到了飞机失事。

options.label: D
options.text: It was postponed to the following day.
options.textZh: 航班被推迟到第二天。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about people's emotions?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士关于人的情绪说了什么?
questions.answerText: They can have an impact as great as rational thinking.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: But even if we think they are ridiculous, emotions can be just as powerful as rational thinking. 但即便我们觉得它们荒唐，情绪也可以和理性思考一样强大。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 让步转折后的主句。女方这句用 even if we think they are ridiculous（让步）退一步，真 正要强调的是转折之后的主句 emotions can be just as powerful as rational thinking， 让步从句是幌子、主句才是观点，正是答案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: emotions can be just as powerful as rational thinking ↔ They can have an impact as great as rational thinking. powerful换成great impact

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 They can be affected by people's childhood experiences. 蹭的是后文 children's dreams 里的"孩子"印象，但那处讲的是"梦"不是"情绪"，且女方没说情绪受童年经历影 响。 借用原文：children's dreams were usually simple representations of their wishes B) 原词陷阱 They may sometimes seem ridiculous to a rational mind. 抓住了原词 we think they are ridiculous，但那只是女方让步退一步说的半句，她真正强调的是转折后的"情绪同样强 大"，只取让步句等于漏掉了观点。 借用原文：even if we think they are ridiculous C) 偷换概念 They usually result from people's unpleasant memories. 录音虽提过 memories，但没 说情绪"源于不愉快的记忆"，unpleasant 是凭空加的限定，与女方所说不符。 借用原文：our dreams are the result of our emotions and memories from that day

options.label: A
options.text: They can be affected by people's childhood experiences.
options.textZh: 情绪可能会受到人童年经历的影响。

options.label: B
options.text: They may sometimes seem ridiculous to a rational mind.
options.textZh: 情绪有时在理性思维看来可能显得荒谬。

options.label: C
options.text: They usually result from people's unpleasant memories.
options.textZh: 情绪通常源于人的不愉快记忆。

options.label: D
options.text: They can have an impact as great as rational thinking.
options.textZh: 情绪可以产生与理性思维同样大的影响。

questions.stem: What did psychologist Sigmund Freud say about adults' dreams?
questions.stemZh: 心理学家Sigmund Freud关于成年人的梦说了什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: But in adults, dreams are much more complicated reflections of their more sophisticated sentiments. 但在成人身上，梦是他们更为复杂精微的情感的、远更复杂的反映。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: But转折切到成人。前句讲 children's dreams… simple representations of their wishes （孩子的梦=愿望），随后 But in adults 用 But 转向成人，这句才是题干问的成人梦，是 答案信号——转折后才是本题落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: dreams are much more complicated reflections of their more sophisticated sentiments ↔ They reflect their complicated emotions. sentiments=emotions改写

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 They call for scientific methods to interpret. 抓的是结尾女方 psychologists try to understand using the scientific method，但那是女方的感叹、谈的是"心理学家研究 梦"，并非弗洛伊德对成人梦的说法。 借用原文：psychologists try to understand using the scientific method B) 原词陷阱 They mirror their long-cherished wishes. 盗用原词 their wishes，但弗洛伊德说"愿 望"指的是 children's dreams（孩子的梦），题问的是成人，对象被偷换。 借用原文：children's dreams were usually simple representations of their wishes D) 张冠李戴 They are often related to irrational feelings. 蹭的是前文 irrational feelings，那是男方 说"人因非理性情绪做疯狂事"，并非弗洛伊德对成人梦下的定性。 借用原文：People do all sorts of crazy things because of their irrational feelings. Section B 1 While some scientists explore the surface of Antarctica, others are learning more about a giant body of water four kilometers beneath the ice pack. Scientists first discovered Lake Vostok in the 1970s by using radio waves that penetrate the ice. Since then, they have used sound waves and even satellites to map this massive body of water. 当一些科学家探索南极洲表面时,其他科学家正在了解更多关于冰层下方四千米处一个巨大水体的信息。科 学家在20世纪70年代首次通过使用能穿透冰层的无线电波发现了沃斯托克湖。此后,他们利用声波甚至卫 星来绘制这个巨大水体的地图。 2 How does the water in Lake Vostok remain liquid beneath an ice sheet? "The thick glacier above acts like an insulating blanket and keeps the water from freezing," says Martin Siegert, a glaciologist from the University of Wales. In addition, geothermal heat from deep within the earth may warm the hidden lake. The scientists suspect that micro-organisms may be living in Lake Vostok, closed off from the outside world for more than 2 million years. 沃斯托克湖中的水如何在冰盖下保持液态?威尔士大学的冰川学家Martin Siegert说:"上方厚厚的冰川就像 一条绝缘毯,防止水结冰。"此外,来自地球深处的地热可能使这个隐藏的湖泊保持温暖。科学家们怀疑微生 物可能生活在沃斯托克湖中,与外界隔绝超过200万年。 3 Anything found there will be totally alien to what's on the surface of the earth, says Siegert. Scientists are trying to find a way to drill into the ice and draw water samples without causing contamination. Again, robots might be the solution. If all goes as planned, a drill-shaped robot will melt through the Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. surface ice. When it reaches the lake, it will release another robot that can swim in the lake, take pictures, and look for signs of life. Siegert说,在那里发现的任何东西都将与地球表面的东西完全不同。科学家们正在努力寻找一种方法来钻 入冰层并抽取水样而不造成污染。机器人可能再次成为解决方案。如果一切按计划进行,一个钻头形状的机 器人将融化表层冰。当它到达湖面时,它将释放另一个可以在湖中游泳、拍照并寻找生命迹象的机器人。 4 The scientists hope their discoveries will shed light on life in outer space, which might exist in similar dark and airless conditions. Recently, close-up pictures of Jupiter's moon, Europa, show signs of water beneath its icy surface. He told Copeland that no amount of money could buy his language. But after Copeland explained to him what he intended to do with his research and how it would benefit the Tarahumaras, Gonzalez agreed to help. He took Copeland to his village and served as an intermediary. Copeland says, "Thanks to him, the Tarahumaras understood what our mission was and started trusting us." 研究美国印第安部落Tarahumaras的想法始于1984年，当时James Copeland发现关于他们语言的研究非 常少。他通过一位在墨西哥与部落成员打交道的社会工作者联系上了一名部落成员。起初，这位名叫 Gonzalez的部落成员非常不愿意合作。他告诉Copeland，再多的钱也买不到他的语言。但在Copeland 向他解释了研究意图以及这将如何使Tarahumaras受益之后，Gonzalez同意帮忙。他带Copeland去了他 的村庄并担任中间人。Copeland说："多亏了他，Tarahumaras理解了我们的使命并开始信任我们。" 2 Entering the world of the Tarahumaras has been a laborious project for Copeland. To reach their homeland he must drive two and a half days from Houston, Texas. He loads up his vehicle with goods that the tribesmen can't easily get, and gives the goods to them as a gesture of friendship. The Tarahumaras, who don't believe in accumulating wealth, take the food and share it among themselves. 进入Tarahumaras的世界对Copeland来说是一个艰苦的项目。要到达他们的家园，他必须从德克萨斯州 休斯顿驱车两天半。他在车上装满部落成员不容易获得的物品，并将这些物品送给他们作为友谊的表示。 不相信积累财富的Tarahumaras接受了食物并在彼此之间分享。 3 For Copeland, the experience has not only been academically satisfying, but also has enriched his life in several ways. "I see people rejecting technology and living a very hard, traditional life, which offers me another notion about the meaning of progress in the western tradition," he says. "I experience the Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard. simplicity of living in nature that I would otherwise only be able to read about. I see a lot of beauty in their sense of sharing and concern for each other." 对Copeland来说，这段经历不仅在学术上令人满意，而且在多方面丰富了他的生活。他说："我看到人们 拒绝技术，过着非常艰苦的传统生活，这为我提供了关于西方传统中进步意义的另一种观念。我体验到生 活在自然中的简单，否则我只能从书中读到。我在他们的分享意识和彼此关心中看到了很多美好。"

analysis.label: 替换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 Their appreciation of help from the outsiders. 原文从未提部落"感激外来者的帮助"；原 文虽讲 Copeland 送礼示好，但被打动的是"分享精神"，而非部落对外人的感激，属无中生 有。 C) 与原文相反 Their readiness to adapt to technology. 盗用了原文的 technology 一词，但原文是 I see people rejecting technology（拒绝技术），选项却说他们"乐于接纳技术"，极性完全 反了。 借用原文：I see people rejecting technology and living a very hard, traditional life D) 与原文相反 Their belief in creating wealth for themselves. 与原文 The Tarahumaras, who don't believe in accumulating wealth 直接矛盾——原文说他们"不相信积累财富"，选项却说他 们"信奉为自己创造财富"，意思反了。 借用原文：The Tarahumaras, who don't believe in accumulating wealth Section C 1 What is a radical? It seems today that people are terrified of the term, particularly of having the label attached to them. Accusing individuals or groups of being radical often serves to silence them into submission, thereby maintaining the existing state of affairs, and, more important, preserving the power of a select minority who are mostly wealthy white males in western society. 什么是激进分子?如今,人们似乎对这个词感到恐惧,尤其是害怕被贴上这样的标签。指责个人或团体是激进 分子往往会让他们沉默并屈服,从而维持现有状态,更重要的是,保护在西方社会中主要由富有的白人男性组 成的少数特权群体的权力。 2 Feminism is a perfect example of this phenomenon. The women's movement has been plagued by stereotypes, misrepresentations by the media, and accusations of man-hating and radicalism, when the basic foundation of feminism is simply that women deserve equal rights in all facets of life. When faced with the threat of being labelled radical, women back down from their worthy calls and consequently participate in their own oppression. 女权主义就是这种现象的完美例证。女性运动一直饱受刻板印象、媒体歪曲报道以及仇恨男性和激进主义 指控的困扰,而女权主义的基本理念不过是女性在生活的各个方面都应享有平等权利。当面临被贴上激进分 子标签的威胁时,女性会从她们正当的诉求中退缩,从而参与到对自身的压迫之中。 Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. 3 It has gotten to the point that many women are afraid to call themselves feminists because of the stigma attached to the word. If people refuse to be controlled and intimidated by stigmas, the stigmas lose all their power. Without fear on which they feed, such stigmas can only die. 事态已发展到许多女性因为这个词所附带的污名而害怕称自己为女权主义者。如果人们拒绝被污名控制和 威胁,这些污名就会失去所有力量。没有了它们赖以生存的恐惧,这些污名只能消亡。 4 To me, a radical is simply someone who rebels against the norm or advocates a change in the existing state of affairs. On close inspection, it becomes clear that the norm is constantly evolving and therefore is not a constant entity. 对我而言,激进分子不过是反抗常规或倡导改变现有状况的人。仔细审视就会发现,常规是不断演变的,因此 并非一个恒定不变的实体。 5 So why then is deviation from the present situation such a threat when the state of affairs itself is unstable and subject to relentless transformation? 那么,既然现有状况本身是不稳定的并且会经历持续不断的变化,为什么偏离当前情况会构成如此大的威胁? 6 It all goes back to maintaining the power of those who have it and preventing the right of those who don't. They are the people about whom history is written. Abolitionists were radicals; civil rights activists were radicals; even the founders of our country in their fight to win independence from England were radicals. Their presence in history has changed the way our society functions, mainly by shifting the balance of power that previously existed. That being said, next time someone calls me a radical, I will accept that label with pride. 这一切都归结于维护拥有权力者的权力,并阻止没有权力者获得权利。事实上,当我们从历史语境审视"激进 分子"这个词时,几乎每一个我们现在奉为英雄的人物在其所处的时代都被视为激进分子。激进分子是促成 变革的人。他们是历史书写的对象。废奴主义者是激进分子;民权活动家是激进分子;甚至我们国家的缔造 者在为赢得独立于英格兰的斗争中也是激进分子。他们在历史中的存在改变了我们社会运作的方式,主要是 通过改变此前存在的权力平衡。当然,也有一些激进分子对人类产生了负面影响,但不可否认的是,没有激进 分子就不会有进步。话虽如此,下次有人称我为激进分子时,我会自豪地接受这个标签。

A) Brains, brains, brains. People are fascinated by brain research. And yet it can be hard to point to places where our education system is really making use of the latest neuroscience( 神经科学) findings. But there is one happy link where research is meeting practice: bilingual(双语的) education. "In the last 20 years or so, there's been a virtual explosion of research on bilingualism," says Judith Kroll, a professor at the University of California, Riverside.
B) Again and again, researchers have found, "bilingualism is an experience that shapes our brain for life," in the words of Gigi Luk, an associate professor at Harvard's Graduate School of Education. At the same time, one of the hottest trends in public schooling is what's often called dual-language or two-way immersion programs.
C) Traditional programs for English-language learners, or ELLs, focus on assimilating students into English as quickly as possible. Dual-language classrooms, by contrast, provide instruction across subjects to both English natives and English learners, in both English and a target language. The goal is functional bilingualism and biliteracy for all students by middle school. New York City, North Carolina, Delaware, Utah, Oregon and Washington state are among the places expanding dual- language classrooms.
D) The trend flies in the face of some of the culture wars of two decades ago, when advocates insisted on "English first" education. Most famously, California passed Proposition 227 in 1998. It was intended to sharply reduce the amount of time that English-language learners spent in bilingual settings. Proposition 58, passed by California voters on November 8, largely reversed that decision, paving the way for a huge expansion of bilingual education in the state that has the largest population of English-language learners.
E) Some of the insistence on English-first was founded on research produced decades ago, in which bilingual students underperformed monolingual(单语的) English speakers and had lower IQ scores. Today's scholars, like Ellen Bialystok at York University in Toronto, say that research was "deeply flawed." "Earlier research looked at socially disadvantaged groups," agrees Antonella Sorace at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland. "This has been completely contradicted by recent research" that compares groups more similar to each other.
F) So what does recent research say about the potential benefits of bilingual education? It turns out that, in many ways, the real trick to speaking two languages consists in managing not to speak one of those languages at a given moment—which is fundamentally a feat of paying attention. Saying "Goodbye" to mom and then "Guten tag" to your teacher, or managing to ask for a crayola roja instead of a red crayon(蜡笔), requires skills called "inhibition" and "task switching." These skills are subsets of an ability called executive function.
G) People who speak two languages often outperform monolinguals on general measures of executive function. "Bilinguals can pay focused attention without being distracted and also improve in the ability to switch from one task to another," says Sorace.
H) Do these same advantages benefit a child who begins learning a second language in kindergarten instead of as a baby? We don't yet know. Patterns of language learning and language use are complex. But Gigi Luk at Harvard cites at least one brain-imaging study on adolescents that shows similar changes in brain structure when compared with those who are bilingual from birth, even when they didn't begin practicing a second language in earnest before late childhood.
I) Young children being raised bilingual have to follow social cues to figure out which language to use with which person and in what setting. As a result, says Sorace, bilingual children as young as age 3 have demonstrated a head start on tests of perspective-taking and theory of mind—both of which are fundamental social and emotional skills.
J) About 10 percent of students in the Portland, Oregon public schools are assigned by lottery to dual- language classrooms that offer instruction in Spanish, Japanese or Mandarin, alongside English. Jennifer Steele at American University conducted a four-year, randomized trial and found that the dual-language students outperformed their peers in English-reading skills by a full school-year's worth of learning by the end of middle school. Because the effects are found in reading, not in math or science where there were few differences, Steele suggests that learning two languages make students more aware of how language works in general.
K) The research of Gigi Luk at Harvard offers a slightly different explanation. She has recently done a small study looking at a group of 100 fourth-graders in Massachusetts who had similar reading scores on a standard test, but very different language experiences. Some were foreign-language dominant and others were English natives. Here's what's interesting. The students who were dominant in a foreign language weren't yet comfortably bilingual; they were just starting to learn English. Therefore, by definition, they had a much weaker English vocabulary than the native speakers. Yet they were just as good at interpreting a text. "This is very surprising," Luk says. "You would expect the reading comprehension performance to mirror the vocabulary—it's a cornerstone of comprehension."
L) How did the foreign-language dominant speakers manage this feat? Well, Luk found, they also scored higher on tests of executive functioning. So, even though they didn't have huge mental dictionaries to draw on, they may have been great puzzle-solvers, taking into account higher-level concepts such as whether a single sentence made sense within an overall storyline. They got to the same results as the monolinguals, by a different path.

Because they are composed of native English speakers deliberately placed together with recent immigrants, they tend to be more ethnically and economically balanced. And there is some evidence that this helps kids of all backgrounds gain comfort with diversity and different cultures. N) Several of the researchers also pointed out that, in bilingual education, non-English-dominant students and their families tend to feel that their home language is heard and valued, compared with a classroom where the home language is left at the door in favor of English. P1 It is not controversial to say that an unhealthy diet causes bad health. Nor are the basic elements of healthy eating disputed. Obesity raises susceptibility to cancer, and Britain is the sixth most obese country on Earth. That is a public health emergency. But naming the problem is the easy part. No one disputes the costs in quality of life and depleted health budgets of an obese population, but the quest for solutions gets diverted by ideological arguments around responsibility and choice. And the water is muddied by lobbying from the industries that profit from consumption of obesity-inducing products.

P2 Historical precedent suggests that science and politics can overcome resistance from businesses that pollute and poison but it takes time, and success often starts small. So it is heartening to note that a programme in Leeds has achieved a reduction in childhood obesity, becoming the first UK city to reverse a fattening trend. The best results were among younger children and in more deprived areas. When 28% of English children aged two to 15 are obese, a national shift on the scale achieved by Leeds would lengthen hundreds of thousands of lives. A significant factor in the Leeds experience Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage. appears to be a scheme called HENRY, which helps parents reward behaviours that prevent obesity in children.

P3 Many members of parliament are uncomfortable even with their own government's anti-obesity strategy, since it involves a "sugar tax" and a ban on the sale of energy drinks to under-16s. Bans and taxes can be blunt instruments, but their harshest critics can rarely suggest better methods. These critics just oppose regulation itself.

P4 The relationship between poor health and inequality is too pronounced for governments to be passive about large-scale intervention. People living in the most deprived areas are four times more prone to die from avoidable causes than counterparts in more affluent places. As the structural nature of public health problems becomes harder to ignore, the complaint about over protective government loses potency.

P5 In fact, the polarised debate over public health interventions should have been abandoned long ago. Government action works when individuals are motivated to respond. Individuals need governments that expand access to good choices. The HENRY programme was delivered in part through children's centres. Closing such centres and cutting council budgets doesn't magically increase reserves of individual self-reliance. The function of a well-designed state intervention is not to deprive people of liberty but to build social capacity and infrastructure that helps people take responsibility for their wellbeing. The obesity crisis will not have a solution devised by left or right ideology—but experience indicates that the private sector needs the incentive of regulation before it starts taking public health emergencies seriously.

P1 Home to virgin reefs, rare sharks and vast numbers of exotic fish, the Coral Sea is a unique haven of biodiversity off the northeastern coast of Australia. If a proposal by the Australian government goes ahead, the region will also become the world's largest marine protected area, with restrictions or bans on fishing, mining and marine farming.

P4 Hugh Possingham, director of the Centre of Excellence for Environmental Decisions at the University of Queensland, points out that little more than half of the Coral Sea reserve is proposed as "no take" area, in which all fishing would be banned. The world's largest existing marine reserve, established last year by the British government in the Indian Ocean, spans 554 000 km² and is a no-take zone throughout. An alliance of campaigning conservation groups argues that more of the Coral Sea should receive this level of protection.

P5 "I would like to have seen more protection for coral reefs," says Terry Hughes, director of the Centre of Excellence for Coral Reef Studies at James Cook University in Queensland. "More than 20 of them would be outside the no-take area and vulnerable to catch-and-release fishing".

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the saying “Beauty of the soul is the essential beauty.” You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.model: The saying "Beauty of the soul is the essential beauty" reminds us that what truly makes a person beautiful is not a pretty face but a noble heart. I fully agree: physical looks may catch the eye, yet it is inner virtue that gives a person lasting worth. Admittedly, an attractive appearance is pleasing and can win instant admiration. However, such charm is transient; wrinkles come and youth fades. Inner beauty, by contrast, endures. Consider a nurse who works tirelessly through the night: her kindness, patience and devotion move us far more deeply than any fashion model's face. It is her character, not her looks, that we remember and respect. History, too, honours people not for how they looked but for the goodness they showed. In conclusion, while outward beauty may fade with time, the beauty of a kind and honest soul only grows brighter. We should therefore cultivate our character rather than obsess over our looks, for it is the soul that makes us truly beautiful.

sentences.text: 语态 「为……所熟知」是中文被动，对应英文被动 be known to sb：are known to almost every Chinese child。这是汉语「为/被……所」结构的标准对译，不可漏掉 be。 时态 回指基调用一般现在时：is、are known——这些故事「至今」仍为孩子熟知，是现状陈述。 单复数与主谓一致 「各种各样妖魔」复数 various demons and monsters；主语若用 the stories（复数）谓语用 are known，若用 the story（单数）则 is known——主谓须一致，别 stories...is。 用词 「妖魔」译 demons and monsters/evil spirits；「几乎每个」almost every + 单数名词（every Chinese child，child 用单数）；「作斗争」fight against/battle against/struggle with。
